stories.title: Nepal floods: A major test for PM Balen's government
stories.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah, an ex-rapper popularly known as "Balen," is facing the enormous task of rebuilding communities and critical infrastructure following last week's deadly flash floods. The floods, carrying rock, ice, mud and debris, swept through areas near the Chinese border, ravaging entire towns and damaging hydropower plants. More than 900 people have been killed and nearly 4,800 remain missing, authorities said Monday, as rescue efforts entered a sixth day. The devastating floods struck the Himalayan nation just days before the anniversary of the Gen-Z-led anti-corruption protests of September 8-9 last year that toppled the previous government and swept Shah to power. Now, the 36-year-old prime minister and his largely inexperienced cabinet face their first major national crisis, in what is shaping up to be the country's worst disaster in a decade. Rescuers, including Chinese and Indian experts, believe hundreds of workers are trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites under construction that were buried in mud by the catastrophic flooding. Sushila Giri was waiting for news of her son, Sishir, a Kathmandu University student completing an internship at one of the hydropower projects. "I came to know that my son, along with others, was at the quarter of the hydro project when the disaster happened," she told DW. "Please help me find his whereabouts." Gen Z activist Raksha Bam expressed concern about delays in rescuing workers trapped at hydropower projects and urged the government to seek specialized assistance from the international community. Across affected districts, family members gathered in hospitals and temporary aid centers hoping for news of missing loved ones. Indra Adhikari lost her home and paddy fields in the floods, while four of her relatives remain missing.

stories.title: Modi-Putin meeting at SCO: Can India-Russia ties hold?
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets Russian President Vladimir Putin in Kyrgyzstan's capital Bishkek on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit — a bloc often seen as a counterweight to US influence. The meeting comes against the backdrop of the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets, and Russia's war in Ukraine, which is in its fifth year. India has remained engaged with the SCO while resisting efforts to turn it into an anti-Western bloc. Its position reflects a broader effort to maintain relationships with competing powers. That approach is under greater pressure. Russiaremains under Western sanctions over the war in Ukraine. Meanwhile, India has faced US pressure over its purchases of Russian oil, alongside wider trade tensions. Former Indian ambassador to the US Meera Shankar told DW that India's relationship with Moscow should not be seen as directed against Washington. "India has a long-standing strategic relationship with Russia. This is not directed against any country but intended to help India meet its national goals," said Shankar. Energy has become the most visible change in the India-Russia relationship since the Ukraine war. Before 2022, when Moscow launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russia supplied only a small share of India's crude imports.

stories.title: Pezeshkian to Modi: Tehran still interested in negotiated solution
stories.summary: Pezeshkian to Modi: Tehran still interested in negotiated solution Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that Tehran is still interested in a negotiated solution to the war with the US, amid renewed hostilities between the two countries. The semi-official Tasnim news agency reports that Pezeshkian met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, telling him that "Iran never welcomes war," but insisting that the US "has not fulfilled its commitments". According to the report, the two leaders discussed maritime cooperation related to the contested Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Bank of Russia projects key rate at 9-11% in 2027 under disinflationary scenario
stories.summary: The key rate is projected at 7-8% in 2028, and at 7.5-8.5% in 2029
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 31.
The Bank of Russia projects the key rate at 14.5-14.6% in 2026, and at 9-11% in 2027 under its disinflationary scenario, the regulator said.
The key rate is projected at 7-8% in 2028, and at 7.5-8.5% in 2029.
The Central Bank also expects inflation at 6-7% in 2026, 3-4% in 2027, and at 4% from 2028 to 2029 under this scenario.
GDP growth is projected at 0-1% in 2026, 2.5-3.5% in 2027, 2-3% in 2028, and 1.5-2.5% in 2029.

stories.title: Some 200 Russian athletes to compete in 2028 Summer Paralympics in US — RPC chief
stories.summary: Pavel Rozhkov revealed that Russia would potentially be represented in 23 sports disciplines
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 31.

Some 200 Russian athletes may participate in the 2028 Summer Paralympic Games in Los Angeles, the United States, while the overall number of the Russian delegation is likely to top 300 people, President of the Russian Paralympic Committee (RPC) Pavel Rozhkov told TASS on Monday.
The RPC chief noted that Russia will potentially be represented in 23 sports disciplines, except for team competitions such as wheelchair basketball, sitting volleyball, wheelchair rugby and boccia.
"It is already necessary to address in detail a number of organizational issues for the successful performance of the national team at the [2028] Paralympics," Rozhkov said.

"These issues include [entry] visa support for all members of the delegation, timely issuance of accreditations, transport logistics, accommodation in the Paralympic Village, which will be located on the University of California campus, organization of meals, developing a training schedule in the United States, as well as medical care and anti-doping control procedures," he continued.
According to him, special attention should be paid to the training schedule on the eve of the Paralympics, as well as to acclimatization details and the time zone gap.

"We must take all of these peculiarities into account in our training plan so that our athletes can focus on the main objective, which is to achieve high results, rather than wasting their energy on everyday routine and coping with climatic conditions," Rozhkov added.
The 2028 Summer Paralympic Games will be hosted by Los Angeles on August 15-27.
